---
title: "Code and history"
description: "Browse project files, open the folder in VS Code, inspect diffs, and restore earlier git snapshots from Fabricator's Code view."
---

Use **Code** when you want to inspect the files behind your app or understand what changed over time. The current Code view is a viewer: it opens project files in a read-only Monaco editor and can open the project folder in VS Code for editing.

![The Code view with the project’s file tree on the left and dashboard.component.tsx open in the read-only editor, with Open in VS Code at the top right.](/screenshots/code.webp)

## Browse files

1. Select **Code** in the project tabs.
2. Select **Files**.
3. Choose a file in the tree.

Fabricator shows project files in a tree and opens text files in the editor. It skips large generated folders such as `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `.vite` and `coverage`.

The editor shows line numbers, syntax highlighting and a minimap. It does not save edits in the current app source. Use **Open in VS Code** when you need to edit a file by hand.

The file header can show:

- The project-relative path.
- The file size.
- **Copy**, which copies the displayed file contents.

If a file is binary, empty, missing or too large to preview, Fabricator shows that message instead of the editor.

## Open files from chat or other views

File chips and file references in chat can open the file in **Code**. The **Blueprint** and **Advisor** views also use the same behavior when they link to source files.

When a line number is provided, Fabricator opens the file and reveals that line in the editor.

## Open the project in VS Code

Select **Open in VS Code** in the Code toolbar. Fabricator runs `code <project-folder>`.

If the `code` command is not available, Fabricator opens the project folder in the operating system file manager instead and shows: "VS Code isn’t installed, so we opened the project folder instead." Use **Get VS Code** from that message if you want to install it.

## Use the git status pill

The project header can show a git pill with the branch and the number of uncommitted changes. When the repository has a remote, it can also show changes to get or push.

Open the pill to use:

- **Get latest** for remote changes waiting to be pulled.
- **Push** for local commits ready to push.
- **Commit all** after entering a **Commit message**.

For team apps, Fabricator saves changes through the team workflow instead of using these local push and pull actions.

## Review history

Select **History** inside **Code** to open the timeline.

![The History tab: a timeline of saved versions, the files changed in the selected version, and a diff of Expense.ts.](/screenshots/history.webp)

The timeline shows saved git snapshots. It also shows **Uncommitted changes** when the working tree has files changed since the last snapshot. Fabricator records snapshots as it works, so this view is the safest way to see what changed without using a terminal.

A project you open from a folder that git doesn't track yet gets a repository when it opens. Its timeline starts with a **Start version history** snapshot. See [Open an existing local project](/docs/build/projects#open-an-existing-local-project).

Select a timeline entry to see:

- The changed files.
- Added, modified, deleted or renamed status.
- Insertions and deletions.
- A text diff for the selected file.

Use **Side by side** or **Unified** to change the diff layout. Use **Wrap** for long lines.

## Compare snapshots

Use **Compare** in the timeline to pick a **Base** snapshot and a **Target** snapshot. Fabricator lists the differences between them.

You can also use **History of this file** from the diff header to jump through the commits that touched the selected file.

## Send history to chat

The History view can stage context in the Build chat:

- **Send to chat** sends the selected snapshot or uncommitted changes.
- **Send comparison** sends the selected base-to-target comparison.
- The chat icon in the diff header sends the selected file's change.

Fabricator switches back to **Build** and places the context in the composer so you can add your own request before sending.

## Restore an earlier version

1. Select an older timeline entry.
2. Select **Restore this version**.
3. Confirm **Restore & redeploy**.

Fabricator saves your current work first if there are uncommitted changes, restores the project to the selected snapshot, records the restore as a new git commit, and then redeploys so the live app matches.

Your current version stays in the timeline, so you can restore it again later. For team apps, restore is scoped to that app's folder; other apps and shared files in the team workspace repository are not restored.
